scope: Independent original-detail eye-contact, identity and source-action review

entries.alt: Jesus and a man look toward one another while the man holds up his restored hand in a synagogue.
entries.caption: Jesus restores a man's hand on the Sabbath. This imagined moment of personal gratitude follows the healing described in Luke; the exact expressions and eye contact are artistic interpretation.
findings: Both heads and visible eyes now face one another at a compatible eye level; Christ's attention clearly meets the man's raised face.
The man's lifted restored hand remains visible and anatomically coherent. His attention has changed from the hand to Christ, so the caption must not say he is examining it.
Approved Christ identity remains recognizable, with natural photographic expression, hair and beard. The secondary man remains distinct.

entries.alt: Jesus faces a man in the temple court, with scattered coins, animals and other people behind them.
entries.caption: This imagined companion scene reflects on Christ's attention to people amid His cleansing of the temple. John records the temple action; this particular face-to-face exchange is an artistic reflection, not a separately recorded conversation.
findings: Christ's head is now inclined toward the opposite man and His eyes settle toward the man's eye/upper-face area; the former elevated gaze beyond him is corrected sufficiently to read as direct personal attention.
The recipient's visible eye faces Christ. This is a credible reciprocal encounter rather than a distant upward look.
Approved identity and sober compassionate expression remain recognizable. Hands, robe, temple setting and distinct secondary face remain coherent; no material new anatomy issue.
